question: Which translator was awarded for translating Anuradha Sharma Pujari's Kanchan (Assamese) into Bodo (awarded in March 2025)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttara Bwiswmuthiary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uttara Bwiswmuthiary** has been honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize 2024** for her translation of the novel **Kanchan** into the **Bodo language**.
 
• The original novel, **Kanchan**, is a highly acclaimed work written in **Assamese** by the renowned author and journalist **Anuradha Sharma Pujari**.
 
• The award was officially conferred in **March 2025** by the **Sahitya Akademi**, which is India's **National Academy of Letters**.
 
• This recognition highlights the importance of **literary exchange** between **Assamese** and **Bodo**, two major languages of **Northeast India**.
 
• The selection for the prize is made based on the recommendations of a **three-member jury** in each language, which is later approved by the **Executive Board** of the **Sahitya Akademi**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Uttara Bwiswmuthiary.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize:**
 
 
• The prize was established in **1989** to encourage the translation of literary works between the **24 languages** recognized by the Akademi.
 
• The award carries a **cash prize of Rs. 50,000** along with an **engraved copper plaque** and a **citation**.
 
• The Akademi recognizes **22 languages** listed in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution**, plus **English** and **Rajasthani**.
 
 
 
• **Anuradha Sharma Pujari:**
 
 
• She is a distinguished **Assamese** novelist and editor of the popular weekly magazine **Sadin** and **Satsori**.
 
• Her novel **Kanchan** is considered a modern classic that explores **socio-economic struggles** and the psychological depth of its protagonist.
 
• She previously won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **2021** for her novel **Iyat Ekhan Aranya Asil**.
 
 
 
• **Bodo Language:**
 
 
• **Bodo** is a **Sino-Tibetan language** spoken primarily by the **Bodo people** of **Assam**.
 
• It was included in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** by the **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **2003**.
 
• It is written using the **Devanagari script**, although it has historically used other scripts as well.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Award:** The translation prize serves to bridge the **cultural gap** between different linguistic communities in India, fostering a **national identity** through shared literature.
 
• **Bodo Literature Growth:** In recent years, **Bodo literature** has seen significant growth, with many young and veteran writers translating classics from **Bengali, Hindi, and Assamese** to enrich the local literary landscape.
 
• **Selection Process:** The **Sahitya Akademi** follows a rigorous **peer-review** and **jury-based** selection process to ensure that only the highest quality translations that preserve the **spirit and nuances** of the original text are rewarded.
 
• **Other Options:** While **Basudeb Das**, **Suvash Satpathy**, and **Anjan Sarma** are names associated with regional literature or translations, they were not the recipients of the **Bodo translation award** for **Kanchan** in the **March 2025** ceremony.
